title: 3.6.8 Lab: Fix a Function That Reassigns Instead of Mutating
description: A function is supposed to update the caller's array but reassigns its parameter instead, so nothing changes. Fix the body so the update reaches the caller. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Run the broken code
steps.instructions: The starter is meant to add 1 to every score in the caller's array. Run it and notice the caller's array comes back unchanged.

steps.title: Find the reassignment
steps.instructions: Inside the function, the parameter is pointed at a brand-new array. That move is local: the caller's variable never follows it.

steps.title: Rewrite the body to mutate
steps.instructions: Change the body so it writes each new value into the array the parameter already points at, using an index. Do not reassign the parameter. Run it and confirm the caller's array now updates.

requirements.title: for loop present
requirements.description: Code contains a for loop. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))

requirements.title: indexed write into the parameter
requirements.description: Code assigns into the array parameter by index. Help: 3.3.3 (Changing an Item by Index)

requirements.title: caller array logged
requirements.description: Code calls console.log on the caller's array. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)

requirements.title: parameter not reassigned
requirements.description: The function writes into the array instead of pointing its parameter at a new one. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)

requirements.title: addOne adds 1 to every score in the caller's array
requirements.description: addOne([10, 20, 30]) changes that same array to [11, 21, 31], and any other array the same way. Help: 3.6.6 (Example: Reassigning Does Not Escape)
requirements.hint: Write into the array the parameter already points at: scores[i] = scores[i] + 1 inside a loop. Do not build a new array.
